themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints have spiked to 17 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 2.0 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 750% increase (z-score: 10.61)—suggesting a sudden proliferation of Uber/Lyft activity or enforcement gaps in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 17 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
750% increase with z-score of 10.61 (extreme statistical anomaly)
Spike is brand-new and concentrated in past 7 days, not a gradual trend
reporting_angles: Interview residents about congestion, illegal pickups, or traffic safety concerns tied to for-hire vehicles
Investigate whether TLC enforcement or city parking/traffic enforcement capacity has changed or declined in the district

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints have skyrocketed to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline average of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—indicating a sudden emergence of unlicensed or problematic street food operations.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
2300% increase with z-score of 8.69 (extreme statistical anomaly)
Correlates with spike in Vendor Enforcement complaints (10 THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 avg, +433%)
reporting_angles: Map which intersections or neighborhoods are seeing the most food vendor activity and identify any unlicensed operations
Interview merchants and residents about whether vendors are creating sanitation, safety, or fair-competition issues

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Bottleneck
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints have surged to 10 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 1.9 per week—a 433% increase (z-score: 5.03)—suggesting residents are reporting unauthorized street vendors faster than the city can regulate them, or enforcement resources are overwhelmed.
evidence: 10 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Spike coincides with mobile food vendor spike (3 complaints THIS WEEK), suggesting both are part of same enforcement crisis
reporting_angles: Interview DOHMH and Dept. of Consumer Affairs about staffing and enforcement capacity in Washington Heights/Inwood
Speak with community board members or residents about whether vendors are perceived as a legitimate safety/quality-of-life issue or an over-complaint phenomenon

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints have jumped to 11 THIS WEEK from a baseline average of 3.6 per week—a 203% increase (z-score: 3.95)—indicating accelerating pavement damage or pothole formation in the district.
evidence: 11 sidewalk condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Community board has repeatedly requested more litter basket collection and street maintenance, suggesting structural infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Conduct a visual audit of sidewalk conditions in high-complaint areas (publish photo evidence)
Investigate whether recent weather events or deferred maintenance have accelerated deterioration; check DOT repair backlogs

themes_detail.label: Public Urination & Street Cleanliness Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Urinating in public complaints have tripled to 3 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 per week (z-score: 4.16), while sidewalk and lot condition complaints are also spiking, pointing to a broader street sanitation and public behavior crisis.
evidence: 3 urinating in public complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% increase)
Coincides with 11 sidewalk condition complaints THIS WEEK (+203%) and dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK (+1100%)
Community board budget requests repeatedly cite park safety and sanitation improvements as unfunded priorities
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners about perceived safety and hygiene conditions on streets and in parks
Investigate whether NYPD or Parks Enforcement has reduced presence or capacity; compare 311 trends to departmental staffing changes
